meta.description: No source shows Patton said it. Wikiquote lists the line as misattributed, and it isn't in his memoir or his published wartime papers.
meta.ogTitle: Who really said 'I'd rather have a German division in front of me than a French one behind me'?
meta.ogDescription: Widely pinned on George S. Patton, but no speech, diary or book of his contains it. Wikiquote lists it as misattributed. Who coined it is unknown.

answer.label: Not George S. Patton — an unsourced attribution
answer.authorDates: Credited to George S. Patton (1885–1945) without evidence
answer.sourceLine: No speech, letter, diary or book of Patton’s has been found that contains this line, and Wikiquote lists it as misattributed ↗. The jab at French allies is a joke with no named originator. It got attached to Patton, who in fact commanded a French armored division in 1944.

source.excerpt: I’d rather have a German division in front of me, than a French one behind.
trail: Wikiquote ↗ lists “I’d rather have a German division in front of me, than a French one behind” under Misattributed. Its note says the line was “Misattributed by former Defense Secretary James Schlesinger on Fox News.”

The same Wikiquote entry points out that Patton commanded French troops. Leclerc’s 2nd Armored Division served under Patton as part of Third Army ↗. Wikiquote describes his relations with Leclerc as “rocky but friendly.”
Quote sites such as AZQuotes ↗ print the line under Patton’s name with no book, speech or date. Quotepark ↗ copies Wikiquote’s misattribution note and asks readers to help find a source.
We searched the text of digitized copies of Patton’s memoir War As I Knew It and of The Patton Papers, 1940–1945 (his diaries and letters, edited by Martin Blumenson). Neither contains the line.
source.excerptNote: This is the wording as Wikiquote lists it, under “Misattributed.” No original context exists to quote, because no documented occasion on which Patton said it has been found.

author.name: George S. Patton
author.heading: About George S. Patton
author.metaLine: 1885–1945 · U.S. Army general, Seventh and Third Armies
author.bio: George S. Patton Jr. was a U.S. Army general. In World War II he commanded the Seventh Army in the Mediterranean and then the Third Army ↗ in France and Germany. His blunt speeches and diaries made him a favorite target for invented one-liners. This line is one of them: he is credited with it, but no source shows he said it.

misattribution.heading: How it got pinned on Patton
misattribution.intro: A soldier’s joke at the expense of French allies is easier to repeat when a famous, blunt-spoken general is named as the speaker. Patton’s reputation for salty one-liners made him the obvious choice, but no record ties this line to him.

items.why: The line is credited to him everywhere but sourced nowhere. Wikiquote ↗ files it under “Misattributed,” and quote sites like AZQuotes ↗ give no speech, book or date.

Wikiquote ↗ says the former Defense Secretary “misattributed” the line to Patton on Fox News. That means he repeated it on air as Patton’s. It does not make Schlesinger the line’s author, and Wikiquote does not say he was.

misattribution.truthLine: No one has traced the line to a documented speaker. Patton’s real dealings with the French included commanding Leclerc’s 2nd Armored Division in Third Army, and Wikiquote ↗ calls those relations “rocky but friendly.”

context.heading: What Patton actually wrote about the French
lead: Patton did command French troops. In August 1944 General Philippe Leclerc’s 2nd Armored Division served under Patton as part of Third Army ↗, and his surviving words about Leclerc are exasperated rather than contemptuous.

In a diary entry dated August 15, 1944, which Wikiquote quotes ↗ right next to the misattributed line, Patton recorded that “Leclerc came in very much excited” and threatened to resign if he could not advance on Paris. Patton wrote: “I told him in my best French that he was a baby,” and the entry ends “We parted friends.”
context.pull: “We parted friends.” — Patton’s diary, on Leclerc

sourcesVerified.claim: Wikiquote lists 'I'd rather have a German division in front of me, than a French one behind.' under the Misattributed section of its Patton page, with the note 'Misattributed by former Defense Secretary James Schlesinger on Fox News.'

The Wikiquote note says Patton commanded French troops (Leclerc's 2nd Armored Division, integrated in the Third Army) and had 'rocky but friendly' relations with him. It quotes an August 15, 1944 diary entry containing 'Leclerc came in very much excited', 'I told him in my best French that he was a baby' and 'We parted friends'.
The French 2nd Armored Division served under General Patton as part of Third Army after landing in August 1944.
Patton commanded the Seventh Army in the Mediterranean, then the Third Army in France and Germany. He was born in 1885 and died in 1945.
AZQuotes credits the line to George S. Patton with no source, book, speech or date.
Quotepark repeats Wikiquote's misattribution note (Schlesinger on Fox News), cites no primary source, and asks readers to help find one.
